mainTopic: The burning of the פר and שעיר, how the Temple learned the שעיר reached the wilderness, and the כהן גדול's reading of the תורה
overview: This amud finishes the ברייתא about where the burned פר and שעיר of יום הכפורים are burned. רבי יוסי requires the בית הדשן. רבא tries to show that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees, and אביי rejects the proof. A second ברייתא teaches that only the one who helps during the actual burning (השורף) has his clothes become טמא, and only until the animals become ash. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון ends the טומאה earlier, and the two opinions differ over a charred mass (חרוכא). Next comes a משנה on how the Temple learned that the שעיר המשתלח had reached the wilderness: signalers on platforms, רבי יהודה's timing method, or רבי ישמעאל's crimson strip turning white. אביי infers that for רבי יהודה the שעיר's מצוה is done once it reaches the wilderness, and the הדרן closes פרק שני שעירי. The new פרק opens with the כהן גדול's reading of the תורה, the eight ברכות after it, and a note that no one could watch both the reading and the burning. The גמרא infers that reading is not an עבודה. It then tries to prove that one may benefit from בגדי כהונה, and each proof is pushed away. The last attempt, about walking in the garments, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where the burned offerings are burned
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with two opinions: north of ירושלים outside three camps, or at the בית הדשן according to רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: North of ירושלים, and outside the three camps. רבי יוסי says: they are burned on the בית הדשן (the place of the ashes).
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing a ברייתא that began on the previous page. It tells us where the פר and שעיר of יום הכפורים are burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gives a location: north of ירושלים and outside all three camps. רבי יוסי adds a requirement: they must be burned on the בית הדשן, a spot where ashes are already found. This raises a question the גמרא will now explore: who argues with רבי יוסי's requirement?

keyTerms.meaning: The three camps (the Divine camp, the Levite camp, the Israelite camp)
The place of ashes, an established ash heap
They are burned
The north side of Jerusalem

phrases.english: To the north of Jerusalem,
and outside the three camps.
phrases.notes: Beyond the Temple, the Levite area, and the Israelite camp.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
They are burned on the place of the ashes.
phrases.notes: A place where ash is already present.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The burned offerings go outside the three camps, north of ירושלים. רבי יוסי requires them to be burned at the בית הדשן.

steps.title: רבא identifies who argues with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the תנא who disagrees with רבי יוסי is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who is the תנא who disagrees with רבי יוסי? It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a claim about who holds the opposing view to רבי יוסי. He is setting up a proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא wants to find a named תנא who does not require ash to already be present at the burning spot. He names רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He will support this from a different ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Which תנא (teacher of the משנה era)?
Who disagrees with him
A תנא, the one רבא identifies

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תְּנָא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי —
phrases.english: Who is the Tanna who disagrees with Rabbi Yosei?
It is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who is the opposing voice to רבי יוסי's opinion in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the תנא who disagrees with רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Proof from the verse about where ashes are poured
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'אל שפך הדשן' two ways: the תנא קמא says ash must already be there, while רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the place must be sloped.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'On the pouring-out of the ashes shall it be burned.' This means there should already be ash there. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: it means its place should be sloped.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to back up his claim. It shows two different readings of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא reads 'שפך הדשן' as 'a place of ash'. That matches רבי יוסי. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads it as 'a sloped place' (משופך), where ash rolls down. רבא assumes this means רבי אליעזר בן יעקב does not require ash to be there already, so he argues with רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The pouring-out place of the ashes (ויקרא ד:יב)
Known as an ash place, with ash already there
Sloped, so things roll downhill

phrases.english: As it was taught:
'On the pouring-out of the ashes shall it be burned,'
that it should be a place of ash (ash already there),
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
that its place should be sloped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's identification in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the one who disagrees with רבי יוסי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא interpreting 'אל שפך הדשן ישרף'. The תנא קמא requires existing ash; רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads it as requiring a slope instead.

steps.title: אביי: maybe they only argue about the slope
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב may also require ash, and the argument is only about whether a slope is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But perhaps it is about whether its place must be sloped that they disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רבא's proof. He shows the ברייתא can be read in a way that does not prove anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rejects the ash requirement. אביי says maybe he agrees ash is needed and simply adds a second requirement, a slope. If so, the only point of argument is the slope, and nobody in that ברייתא argues with רבי יוסי about the ash.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (a typical opening for a rejection)
That they disagree
He said to him

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agrees with the תנא קמא on everything. He says they may agree on the ash and argue only about the slope. The proof fails, but the argument in that ברייתא still exists.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But perhaps, about its place being sloped,
is what they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא. It does not disprove רבא's identification itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed that requiring a slope means not requiring ash. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב may require both.

steps.title: Only the one who burns has his clothes become impure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches from 'והשורף' that the burner's clothes become טמא, but not those of the one who lights the fire or arranges the wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And he who burns them.' The one who burns makes his garments impure. The one who lights the fire does not, and the one who arranges the woodpile does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a new ברייתא. It deals with who becomes טמא through the burning of the פר and שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא טז:כח) says 'והשורף אותם יכבס בגדיו'. The ברייתא reads 'השורף' narrowly. Only the actual burner is affected. Those who do preparation work, like lighting the fire or arranging the wood, are excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
The one who burns
Makes his clothing impure
The one who lights the fire
The one who arranges the woodpile

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a clear limit on who becomes טמא. Being near the burning or helping set it up is not enough.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'And he who burns' —
the one who burns makes garments impure,
but not the one who lights the fire,
and not the one who arranges the woodpile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, unrelated to the location debate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the burner's clothes become טמא. The fire-lighter's and wood-arranger's clothes do not.

steps.title: Who counts as the one who burns
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how to define 'השורף'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the one who burns?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for a definition. It is setting up its answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lighting the fire and arranging the wood have been excluded. So the ברייתא now needs to say exactly which actions make someone 'the burner'. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: And who is this?

phrases.english: And who is the one who burns?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact definition of 'השורף' for the law of טומאת בגדים.

steps.title: The one who helps during the burning
steps.stepSummary: 'השורף' is anyone who assists while the burning is actually taking place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the one who assists at the time of the burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. 'The burner' is whoever helps during the burning itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is timing. Help given before the burning starts, like lighting the fire or setting the wood, does not count. Help given while the animal is burning does count, and that person's clothes become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who assists
At the time of the burning

steps.whatToRemember: Only someone who helps during the actual burning has his clothes become טמא. Lighting the fire and arranging the wood beforehand do not count.

phrases.english: It is the one who assists at the time of the burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'השורף' is whoever assists during the actual burning.

steps.title: Once the animals become ash, they no longer make clothes impure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The word 'אותם' limits the טומאה to the animals themselves, not their ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the clothes become impure even after the animals have turned to ash. So the verse says 'them.' 'Them' makes clothes impure, but once they have become ash they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from the definition of 'השורף'. Now it asks how long the burning animals keep making clothes טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests that the טומאה might last all the way through, even after the animals become ash. The extra word 'אותם' ('them') points to the animals in their real form. So once they are ash, the person handling them no longer gets טמא clothes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': it introduces a mistaken assumption that the verse will correct
'The verse teaches': it introduces the word in the פסוק that settles the question
'Them': the word in the verse that limits the טומאה to the animals themselves
Ash
They make clothes ritually impure

phrases.english: One might think that even once they have become ash
they make clothes impure
therefore the verse says: 'them'
phrases.notes: From the verse והשורף אותם יכבס בגדיו (ויקרא טז:כח), the same verse that gave us 'והשורף' in step 5

phrases.english: 'them,' the animals themselves, make clothes impure
but not once they have become ash
do they make clothes impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף מִשֶּׁנַּעֲשׂוּ אֵפֶר מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אוֹתָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining who counts as 'השורף', the ברייתא now sets the end point in time of the טומאה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פר and שעיר make the burner's clothes טמא only until they become ash.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the טומאה stops once the flesh is burned through
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון sets an earlier cutoff: once the flesh is burned through, the clothes no longer become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: the bull makes things impure, but once the flesh is burned through, it no longer makes clothes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different end point for the טומאה. He sets it earlier than ash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the טומאה lasts until the animal is ash. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it stops as soon as the flesh is burned through. That happens before it is fully ash. This sets up the question of where exactly the two opinions differ.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull (here, the פר of יום הכיפורים)
The flesh has been burned through (melted away by the fire)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
the bull makes things impure,
but once the flesh is burned through
it no longer makes clothes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion within the same ברייתא about when the טומאה ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טומאה ends once the flesh is burned through, even before it becomes ash.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical case where the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would rule differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks in which real case the two opinions give different results. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Burned flesh' and 'ash' sound almost the same. So the גמרא wants a concrete case where they come apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is between them?': what is the practical difference between the two opinions

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how step 8 and step 9 differ in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The concrete case where the תנא קמא (ash) and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון (burned flesh) disagree

steps.title: The difference is a charred animal that is not yet ash
steps.stepSummary: The difference is when the animal has become a charred mass but is not yet ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is when he turned it into a charred mass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The two opinions differ when the animal is charred but not yet ash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A charred animal has lost its normal form, so its flesh is already burned through. According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, it no longer makes clothes טמא. According to the תנא קמא, it still does, because it has not yet become ash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is a difference between them': this introduces the practical case
A charred, scorched mass, burned but not yet ash

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא: clothes become טמא until the animal is ash. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: only until the flesh is burned through. They differ about a charred animal (חרוכא).

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he turned it into a charred mass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A charred animal that is not yet ash: it is טמא according to the תנא קמא and טהור according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: New משנה: signalers on platforms announce that the goat reached the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. The כהן גדול is told that the שעיר has reached the wilderness. People knew this from cloths waved by signalers standing on platforms along the route.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to the כהן גדול: the goat has reached the wilderness. How did they know the goat had reached the wilderness? They built platforms and waved cloths, and so they knew the goat had reached the wilderness.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes how word reached the בית המקדש that the שעיר המשתלח had arrived in the wilderness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states the fact and then explains how it was known. People stood on platforms set up along the road. Each one waved a cloth, passing the signal back step by step to ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה: a new section of the משנה begins here
The High Priest
The goat (the שעיר המשתלח, sent to עזאזל)
Raised platforms or stations along the road
Scarves or cloths, waved as a signal

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
They said to the High Priest:
the goat has reached the wilderness.
And how did they know
that the goat had reached the wilderness?
They would build platforms
and wave cloths.
And so they knew that the goat had reached the wilderness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל: הִגִּיעַ שָׂעִיר לַמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It changes subject from the burning to the arrival of the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול is told when the שעיר reaches the wilderness. This was known from signalers waving cloths on platforms.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a simple timing calculation was enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argues that no platforms were needed. The distance was three מיל, so timing alone showed when the goat had arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: Didn't they have a clear sign? From ירושלים to בית חדודו is three מיל. They walk a מיל, come back a מיל, and wait the time of another מיל. Then they know the goat has reached the wilderness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the platform method. He offers a simpler way to know: measure the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The escorts walk out one מיל with the man leading the goat, then walk one מיל back. That is two מיל of time. They wait the time it takes to walk one more מיל. That makes three מיל in total, the exact distance to the wilderness, so the goat must have arrived.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But surely': this introduces a challenge to what was just said
A sign or indicator
The place at the edge of the wilderness where the goat was sent off
A unit of distance (about 2,000 אמות)
They wait

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא: signalers on platforms announced the goat's arrival. רבי יהודה: the timing of walking a מיל out, a מיל back, and waiting one more מיל was already a clear sign.
steps.confusionAlert: The people of ירושלים did not walk the full three מיל. They walked only one מיל out and one back, then waited. The time adds up to three מיל, which is how long the goat needed to reach בית חדודו.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
But didn't they have a clear sign?
From Jerusalem until Beit Chadodo
is three mil.
They walk a mil and return a mil,
and wait the time it takes to walk a mil,
and then they know that the goat has reached the wilderness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וַהֲלֹא סִימָן גָּדוֹל הָיָה לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view within the משנה. It challenges the need for the platforms described in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There was no need for platforms. The time it takes to walk three מיל showed that the goat had reached the wilderness.

steps.title: A third sign: the crimson strip turned white
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says there was another sign: a crimson strip tied at the היכל turned white when the שעיר reached the wilderness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: Didn't they have a different sign? A strip of crimson wool was tied on the entrance of the היכל. When the שעיר reached the wilderness, the strip turned white, as the פסוק says: 'If your sins are like scarlet, they will become white as snow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third opinion on how they knew the שעיר had reached the wilderness. רבי ישמעאל points to a miracle: a crimson strip that turned white.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא used signalers waving cloths, and רבי יהודה used timing. רבי ישמעאל says neither was needed because there was a visible miracle in the מקדש itself. The strip turning white showed that the sins of ישראל were forgiven, as in the פסוק in ישעיה.

keyTerms.meaning: A strip of crimson (red) wool
The Sanctuary building in the בית המקדש
Turns white
A sign or indicator

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the physical sending of the שעיר to the spiritual result, which is כפרה (forgiveness). Everyone could see that the sins had been made 'white as snow.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
But didn't they have a different sign?
A strip of crimson wool

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה קָשׁוּר עַל פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל,
phrases.english: was tied on the entrance of the Sanctuary,
and when the goat reached the wilderness
the strip would turn white,
phrases.notes: A miracle showing that the sins were forgiven.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"If your sins are like scarlet,
they will become white as snow"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third way of knowing, alongside the signalers of the תנא קמא and the timing method of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A crimson strip at the היכל turned white when the שעיר reached the wilderness. That was the sign.

steps.title: אביי's inference from רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from רבי יהודה's timing method that בית חדודו is in the wilderness, and that the שעיר's מצוה is done once it reaches the wilderness.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: אביי said: Learn from this that בית חדודו is located in the wilderness. And this teaches us that רבי יהודה holds that once the שעיר reaches the wilderness, its מצוה is complete.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens on this משנה with אביי drawing two conclusions from רבי יהודה's statement (step 13).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה measured the trip to בית חדודו and called that 'reaching the wilderness.' So בית חדודו itself must count as the wilderness. He also treated arrival as the moment to signal, before the goat is pushed off the cliff. That shows he holds the מצוה is already complete on arrival.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (an inference)
A place on the route, three מיל from ירושלים
It teaches us
Its מצוה has been done

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the goat is not pushed off the cliff. It still is. The point is only that the מצוה counts as done once the goat reaches the wilderness, so the כהן גדול may go on with the service without waiting.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the moment the כהן גדול may continue with the next part of the service, which is the next פרק.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Abaye said:
Learn from this
that Beit Chiddudo is located in the wilderness,
and this is what it teaches us:
that Rabbi Yehuda holds:
once the goat has reached the wilderness
its מצוה is complete.
phrases.notes: Even before it is pushed off the cliff.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יהודה's view (step 13) and draws conclusions from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית חדודו counts as the wilderness. According to רבי יהודה, the שעיר's מצוה is complete as soon as it reaches the wilderness.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the מצוה of the שעיר is done on arrival in the wilderness, and בית חדודו is already the wilderness.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of the two goats
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק שני שעירי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'The Two Goats.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the sixth פרק, שני שעירי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell to a finished chapter. It shows that the discussion of the שעיר המשתלח is finished. A new topic comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
'The Two Goats', the name of the chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'The Two Goats'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that step 15 finished.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter on the two goats is finished.

steps.title: New chapter: what the כהן גדול wears to read the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens: the כהן גדול comes to read from the תורה. He may read in the linen priestly garments or in his own white robe.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן גדול came to read. If he wanted to read in the בגדי בוץ, he reads in them. If not, he reads in a white robe of his own.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins. Now that the שעיר has reached the wilderness, the כהן גדול moves on to read from the תורה, and the משנה tells us what he may wear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading comes after the שעיר's מצוה is complete, which links back to step 15. The משנה gives him a choice: the priestly linen garments or his own white robe. The גמרא will soon infer from this choice that the reading is not an עבודה (step 22).

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest
The white linen priestly garments of יום הכיפורים
A white robe
His own, not from the הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume he must stay in the special priestly clothes. The reading is not a service, so his own white robe is allowed.

phrases.english: The High Priest came to read,

phrases.aramaic: אִם רָצָה לִקְרוֹת בְּבִגְדֵי בוּץ — קוֹרֵא,
phrases.english: if he wished to read in the linen garments, he reads in them;
and if not,
he reads in a white robe of his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול may read from the תורה either in the linen priestly garments or in his own white robe.

steps.title: The ספר תורה is passed up to the כהן גדול, who reads
steps.stepSummary: The scroll goes from the חזן הכנסת to the ראש הכנסת, then to the סגן, then to the כהן גדול. He stands, receives it, and reads אחרי מות and אך בעשור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חזן הכנסת takes a ספר תורה and gives it to the ראש הכנסת. The ראש הכנסת gives it to the סגן, and the סגן gives it to the כהן גדול. The כהן גדול stands, receives it, and reads the sections of אחרי מות and אך בעשור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing the reading it introduced in Step 17. It explains who hands the scroll to the כהן גדול and what he reads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll passes through several officials of rising rank before it reaches the כהן גדול. This honors him in front of the whole crowd. He reads two passages from ויקרא that describe the יום כיפור service and the day's laws.

keyTerms.meaning: The synagogue attendant or caretaker (not a cantor here)
The head of the synagogue
The deputy כהן גדול, second in rank
ויקרא chapter 16, which describes the יום כיפור service
ויקרא 23:26–32, the laws of יום כיפור

steps.confusionAlert: Here חזן does not mean the person who leads the prayers. It means the synagogue attendant who handles the scroll.

phrases.english: The synagogue attendant takes a Torah scroll,
and gives it to the head of the synagogue,
and the head of the synagogue gives it to the deputy High Priest,
and the deputy gives it to the High Priest,
and the High Priest stands and receives it,
and reads "After the death" and "But on the tenth",

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the כהן גדול's Torah reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scroll is handed up a chain of honor to the כהן גדול, who stands and reads אחרי מות and אך בעשור.

steps.title: He rolls the scroll and recites the third section by heart
steps.stepSummary: After reading, the כהן גדול rolls up the scroll, holds it, and announces that more is written there than he read. He then recites ובעשור from ספר במדבר by heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: He rolls the ספר תורה, places it in his lap, and says: "More than what I read before you is written here." The section of ובעשור in ספר במדבר he recites by heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the כהן גדול handles the third required reading. He does not roll the scroll to it. He says it from memory instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third section, ובעשור, is in במדבר, far away in the scroll. Rolling to it in front of the crowd would cause a long delay, so he recites it by heart. His announcement tells the people that this section really is written in the תורה, even though he is not reading it from the scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: Rolls up the scroll
ספר במדבר ("the book of the countings")
By heart, from memory

phrases.aramaic: וְגוֹלֵל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה וּמַנִּיחוֹ בְּחֵיקוֹ וְאוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And he rolls up the Torah scroll, places it in his lap, and says:
More than what I have read before you
is written here.
The section "And on the tenth" in the Book of Numbers
he recites by heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading by explaining how the third section is handled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The section of ובעשור in במדבר is recited by heart, after he announces that more is written in the scroll.

steps.title: The eight blessings after the reading
steps.stepSummary: After the reading, the כהן גדול recites eight ברכות. They cover the תורה, the עבודה, thanksgiving, forgiveness of sin, the מקדש, ישראל, ירושלים, the כהנים, and the rest of the prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He recites eight ברכות over it: on the תורה, on the עבודה, on thanksgiving, on forgiveness of sin, on the מקדש by itself, on ישראל by themselves, on ירושלים by itself, on the כהנים by themselves, and on the rest of the prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the ברכות the כהן גדול says after reading. This list closes the reading ceremony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some ברכות resemble the ones we say every day: the ברכה after the Torah reading, רצה, מודים, and a ברכה for forgiveness. Others are special requests for the מקדש, ישראל, ירושלים, and the כהנים. The words "by itself" mean that each of these gets its own separate ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple service (the ברכה of רצה)
Thanksgiving (the ברכה of מודים)
Forgiveness of sin
As a separate ברכה of its own
General requests, ending with "Who hears prayer"

steps.confusionAlert: If you count the items in this list, you may get more than eight. Versions of the text and the commentators differ on how to count them. Don't let the count stop you; focus on the topics of the ברכות.

phrases.english: And he recites over it eight blessings:
on the Torah, and on the Temple service,
and on thanksgiving, and on forgiveness of sin,
and on the Temple by itself,
and on Israel by themselves,
and on Jerusalem by itself,
and on the priests by themselves,
and on the rest of the prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reading itself to the ברכות said after it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the reading, the כהן גדול recites eight ברכות on the listed topics.

steps.title: No one could watch both the reading and the burning
steps.stepSummary: A person who watched the כהן גדול read could not also watch the burning of the פר and שעיר, and the reverse. This was not forbidden. The two places were far apart, and both events happened at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees the כהן גדול reading does not see the פר and שעיר being burned. One who sees the פר and שעיר being burned does not see the כהן גדול reading. This is not because it is forbidden, but because the way between them was long, and both were done at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a practical note about what onlookers could see. It explains that the two events overlapped in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first states that no one saw both events. It then makes clear that this was a matter of distance and timing, not a prohibition. The burning took place outside the city while the reading was happening in the Temple, at the same moment.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull and goat of יום כיפור, which are burned outside the city
Permitted
A distant path, a long way

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with a factual note. You could not attend both events because of distance and timing, not because of any prohibition.

phrases.english: One who sees the High Priest when he is reading
does not see the bull and goat that are burned,
and one who sees the bull and goat that are burned

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל כְּשֶׁהוּא קוֹרֵא.
phrases.english: does not see the High Priest when he is reading.
And not because he is not permitted,
but because it was a distant path,
and the performance of both of them takes place at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with a note on timing and onlookers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Watching both events was permitted, but it was impossible because of the distance and the overlapping timing.

steps.title: The גמרא infers that קריאת התורה is not an עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה lets the כהן גדול read in his own white robe. From this it infers that reading the תורה is not counted as an עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Since the משנה teaches that he may read in a white robe of his own, we learn by inference that reading is not an עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a דיוק, an inference, from the wording of the משנה in Step 17. This sets up the next move, which looks at the other option of reading in the בגדי בוץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every true עבודה must be done in the בגדי כהונה. The משנה allows the reading in a private robe, so the reading must not be an עבודה. The משנה also allowed reading in the בגדי בוץ, and that will raise the next question: may a כהן benefit from the priestly garments when he is not doing an עבודה?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
His own private white robe
By inference, implied from

steps.whyThisMatters: This inference starts the גמרא's discussion of whether one may benefit from בגדי כהונה outside of the עבודה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From the fact that it teaches "in a white robe of his own,"
we infer that reading is not a Temple service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by drawing an inference from the משנה's permission to read in a private robe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah reading is not an עבודה, since it may be done without the priestly garments.

steps.title: Reading in priestly garments suggests one may benefit from them
steps.stepSummary: Reading is not an עבודה, yet the משנה lets the כהן גדול read in his בגדי בוץ. So it seems one may benefit from בגדי כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the משנה teaches: if he wants to read in his white linen garments, he may read. You can learn from this that the priestly garments were given to be used for one's own benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the conclusion of step 22 (reading is not an עבודה) and uses it to try to prove a bigger rule about בגדי כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally בגדי כהונה are holy and meant only for the עבודה. If the כהן גדול may wear them for something that is not an עבודה, then wearing them outside the עבודה must be allowed. That would mean they 'were given for benefit'.

keyTerms.meaning: White linen garments of the כהן גדול worn on יום הכיפורים
Priestly garments
To benefit, to use for personal purposes
You can learn from this, a proof formula

phrases.english: And it teaches:
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's line about reading.

phrases.aramaic: אִם רָצָה לִקְרוֹת בְּבִגְדֵי בוּץ — קוֹרֵא,
phrases.english: If he wants to read in linen garments, he reads,
learn from this
that priestly garments were given to be benefited from!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 22 (reading is not an עבודה) to infer a general rule.
steps.raayaObject: That one may benefit from בגדי כהונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting the כהן גדול to read in בגדי בוץ, combined with step 22's point that reading is not an עבודה.

steps.title: Reading may be different because it serves the עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. Reading is not itself an עבודה, but it is done for the needs of the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps reading is different, because it is for the need of the עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something can fail to count as a real עבודה and still be connected to the day's service. The reading of יום הכיפורים belongs to that service, so wearing the garments for it is not 'personal benefit'. The case proves nothing about wearing them for purely private use.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, a typical opener for rejecting a proof
Is different
A need of the Temple service

steps.confusionAlert: Step 22 said reading is not an עבודה, and that still stands. 'צורך עבודה' is a different idea: the reading is not the service itself, but it is connected to it.

phrases.english: Perhaps reading is different
since it is for the need of the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Reading is tied to the עבודה, so it is not a case of purely personal benefit.

steps.title: Background: the open question about benefiting from priestly garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why it tried this proof. It was an open question whether one may benefit from בגדי כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For it was asked of us: were the priestly garments given to be benefited from, or were they not given to be benefited from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the question that the last two steps were trying to answer. This sets up a series of attempted proofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. Either the garments may be worn for ordinary use, or they are only for the עבודה. Every proof that follows tries to settle this question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of us; an unresolved question
Were given (by the תורה) for this use
Benefit, personal use

phrases.english: For it was asked of us:
were priestly garments given to be benefited from,
or were they not given to be benefited from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wider question behind the proof attempt of steps 23–24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בגדי כהונה may be worn for personal benefit.

steps.title: Proof from sleeping: they did not sleep in them, so they could eat in them
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says כהנים did not sleep in the holy garments. That implies eating in them was allowed, which would show that benefit is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: they would not sleep in the holy garments. Sleeping is what is not allowed, but eating, they would eat in them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new attempt to answer the question from a משנה about sleeping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids only sleeping. So the גמרא reads it as allowing other activities, such as eating. Eating is not an עבודה, so this would show that benefit from the garments is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introduces a proof
Holy garments, meaning the priestly garments
Sleep
Eating

phrases.english: Come and hear:
They would not sleep in the holy garments.
It is sleep that is not allowed,
but eating, they eat!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לֹא הָיוּ יְשֵׁנִים בְּבִגְדֵי קוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof attempt for the question of step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That one may benefit from בגדי כהונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'לא היו ישנים בבגדי קודש', read as implying that eating was allowed.

steps.title: Eating may be different because eating קדשים brings כפרה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. When כהנים eat the קרבנות, that eating is part of the עבודה, because it brings כפרה to the owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps eating is different, because it is for the need of the עבודה. As a ברייתא teaches: 'And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made.' This teaches that the כהנים eat and the owners receive כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the eating proof, the same way it pushed away the reading proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים' eating of קדשים is part of the כפרה process, as a ברייתא shows from the פסוק. So eating in the garments is a צורך עבודה and not private benefit. The question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches
The owners of the קרבן
Receive atonement

phrases.english: Perhaps eating is different
since it is for the need of the service,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
'And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made' —
this teaches that the priests eat
and the owners achieve atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא שָׁאנֵי אֲכִילָה דְּצוֹרֶךְ עֲבוֹדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 26, using the same reasoning as step 24.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Eating קדשים is itself part of the כפרה, so it counts as a צורך עבודה.

steps.title: Second inference: they could walk in the garments
steps.stepSummary: From the same משנה the גמרא infers that walking around in the garments was allowed. Walking has no link to the עבודה, so this would prove that benefit is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sleeping is what is not allowed, but walking around, they would walk in them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the same משנה and draws a different inference, one that the צורך עבודה answer cannot push away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking around is not a צורך עבודה at all. If walking in the garments is allowed, that must be because personal benefit is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Walking around
They walk
But (implied), used to draw an inference

phrases.english: It is sleep that is not allowed,
but walking, they walk!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֵׁינָה הוּא דְּלָא, הָא הַלּוֹכֵי מְהַלְּכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same משנה as step 26 to draw a new inference that avoids the rejection in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That one may benefit from בגדי כהונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implication of 'לא היו ישנים בבגדי קודש'.

steps.title: Really, walking is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The inference is rejected. By right, walking in the garments is also not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right, walking around is also not allowed,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא denies the inference. The משנה does not mean that walking is allowed. The explanation of why the משנה mentions only sleeping continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not accept that 'only sleep is forbidden'. Walking is forbidden too. So the משנה's silence about walking does not prove that benefit is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: By right, strictly speaking
Also
Not (allowed)

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is cut off. The next passage explains why the משנה mentions only sleeping, so do not treat this line as the full answer yet.

phrases.english: By right, walking too is not allowed,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the walking inference of step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that walking is allowed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's wording does not exclude walking. Walking is also forbidden.
